# The exact identical-inner-pair certificate fails on four triangle fibers

Let `T=T_2` be the standard triangle and `V=|T|`. For a diagonal
point `y=a(1,1)`, the ordinary depth of `rT`, divided by `V`, is

    F_r(a)=4a min(a,(r-2a)_+)             for a>=0.             (1)

For a positive concave radius sequence on a complete integer interval,
the proposed certificate at anchor `j` is

    C_j(a)=F_(r_j)(a)+2 sum_(h>=1) F_(rho_h)(a),
    rho_h=min(r_(j-h),r_(j+h)),
    0<=a<=r_j/2,                                             (2)

where pairs with a missing endpoint are omitted. Although `V C_j(a)`
is a valid lower bound for actual mixed depth, it need not reach
`(2/9)V sum_k r_k^2`, even after optimizing EVERY anchor and point.

## 1. An exact rational counterexample

At bases `0,1,2,3`, take radii

    (r_0,r_1,r_2,r_3)=(1,2,2,1).                             (3)

Their differences are `1,0,-1`, so they are concave and positive.
Linearly interpolate this radius roof between consecutive integer
bases. The body

    { (z,x): 0<=z<=3, x_1,x_2>=0, x_1+x_2<=r(z) }

is full-dimensional and convex, is the convex hull of the four lifted
triangles, and has exactly their prescribed positive integer fibers.
Thus this is an actual convex-compatible chain, not merely a sequence
of independently assigned masses.

At either endpoint anchor, the certificate has only its own term, with
maximum `4/9`. At either inner anchor there is exactly one reflected
pair, of common inner radius one. Hence it is

    C(a)=F_2(a)+2F_1(a),       0<=a<=1.

Its COMPLETE piecewise expression is

    12a^2,                    0<=a<=1/3;
    8a-12a^2,                 1/3<=a<=1/2;
    4a^2,                     1/2<=a<=2/3;
    8a-8a^2,                  2/3<=a<=1.                    (4)

The first piece increases to `4/3`. The second is nonincreasing from
that value, since its vertex is `a=1/3`. The third increases to
`16/9`; the fourth decreases from that value, since its quadratic
vertex is `a=1/2`, outside that piece. Consequently

    max_(j,a) C_j(a)=16/9 <20/9=(2/9) sum_k r_k^2.            (5)

All four anchors and every allowed real `a` have been included.
The maximizing inner points in (5) are their actual own centroids,
`a=2/3`, where the reflected inner-triangle payment vanishes entirely.

## 2. A full family and a stronger integer-radius instance

More generally take radii `(1,R,R,1)` for any `R>=3/2`. The inner
certificate is `F_R(a)+2F_1(a)` on `0<=a<=R/2`. Its four pieces are

    12a^2,                    0<=a<=1/3;
    8a-12a^2,                 1/3<=a<=1/2;
    4a^2,                     1/2<=a<=R/3;
    4Ra-8a^2,                 R/3<=a<=R/2.                  (6)

An empty middle interval at `R=3/2` causes no exception. The same
monotonicity calculation proves the exact all-anchor maximum

    max_(j,a) C_j(a)=max{4/3,4R^2/9}.                         (7)

The target is `4(R^2+1)/9`, which exceeds BOTH terms of (7) for
every `R>=3/2`. The ratio of the exact optimized certificate to its
target is

    max{3,R^2}/(R^2+1).

Within this family its minimum is exactly `3/4`, attained at
`R=sqrt(3)`. This is a statement about the certificate, not an
optimized mixed-depth ratio.

The fully rational choice `R=7/4`, followed by scaling all radii by
four, gives the integer radius profile

    (4,7,7,4),
    max_(j,a) C_j(a)=196/9,
    (2/9) sum_k r_k^2=260/9.

Its exact ratio is `49/65`, and the strict shortfall is `64/9`.
All vertices of these four original triangles are integral.

## 3. The certificate is valid; its claimed sufficiency is what fails

For each reflected pair, the two actual fibers contain identical
copies of `rho_h T` at their original bases. The single actual cap
through `(j,a(1,1))` induces the same normal and opposite offsets on
these two copies. The proved all-point identical-triangle identity
therefore gives at least `2V F_(rho_h)(a)` from that pair. If the point
is outside the inner triangle, the right side is zero and the lower
bound remains valid. The own fiber contributes `V F_(r_j)(a)`.
These source fibers are disjoint, so adding the payments gives (2).

A vertical closed cap includes the whole own fiber and at least one
member of each reflected pair. Its corresponding mass is at least
`V[r_j^2+sum rho_h^2]`, which dominates (2), since every ordinary
triangle depth is at most `Gamma_2` times its area and
`2Gamma_2=8/9<1`. Thus no vertical exception explains (5).

The pointwise layer-cake identity

    F_r(a)=4a integral_(2a)^(3a) 1_(r>=s) ds

also remains correct. At levels whose radius superlevel interval does
not contain `j`, its reflected count is zero: two reflected members
would force the interval to contain their midpoint. At the other
levels, this count is the largest symmetric subinterval about `j`.
Thus the counterexample directly rejects sufficiency of that exact
layer-cake functional, without replacing its level intervals or moving
the anchor separately between levels.

## 4. Exact finite optimization, with no omitted interior stationary points

For any fixed anchor, form the multiset consisting of its own radius
with multiplicity one and each inner pair radius with multiplicity two.
The certificate is a sum of the functions (1). Its only breakpoints
are `r/3` and `r/2` for these radii. On any open interval between
successive breakpoints, let `n_H` be the weighted count with `r>=3a`,
let `n_M` be the weighted count with `2a<r<3a`, and let `R_M` be
the weighted sum of the latter radii. Then

    C_j(a)=(4n_H-8n_M)a^2+4R_M a.

The maximum on that interval is attained at an endpoint, or, if its
quadratic coefficient is negative, at

    a=R_M/(4n_M-2n_H)

when this value lies in the interval. The functions agree at all
breakpoints, despite their possible derivative jumps. This gives an
exact rational procedure for every anchor and every real parameter;
it is the procedure implemented in the verifier.

## 5. The actual source is OC-safe

The four-fiber equal-middle theorem already applies to `(T,2T,2T,T)`.
More explicitly, its proved three-source subset payment at the first
middle centroid uses the first three fibers `T,2T,2T` and gives

    Gamma_2 |2T|+|T|/2=(41/18)V>(20/9)V.

The fourth fiber adds nonnegative cap mass. This is an all-orientation
bound from `candidate 24b9a17cce573038`
and its underlying measurable-subset theorem. It is not obtained by
the failed reflected-inner-pair certificate. The same four-fiber
theorem covers every member of (6).

The result is therefore an exact obstruction to this auxiliary
certificate, not an OC counterexample and not a failure of the
identical-triangle paired identity.

The standard-library verifier is
`../assets/pk-nov6/computations/verify_triangle_chain_inner_pair_certificate_failure.py`.
